intro: North Dakota runs elections county by county, through the county auditor, and has no voter registration.

id_rule.text: Bring a valid ID that shows your name, current North Dakota address, and date of birth, such as a North Dakota driver's license or non-driver ID, or a tribal ID. Digital IDs are not accepted. If you have no valid ID with you, you can vote a set-aside ballot, and you have 13 days after the election to show your ID to the county auditor.

elections.name: General election
elections.hours: Set by each county. Polls open between 7:00 am and 9:00 am and close between 7:00 pm and 9:00 pm, local time.
elections.what: Federal, state and local offices, plus any statewide or local measures. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: Early voting can begin
dates.detail: Each county decides whether to offer early in-person voting, starting up to 15 days before Election Day. In 2026 these counties offer it: Burleigh, Cass, Grand Forks, Morton, Stark, Stutsman, and Ward. Dates and times vary.

src.label: North Dakota Secretary of State, 2026 general election key information

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Poll hours vary by county. If you are in line when the polls close, you can still vote. North Dakota has no voter registration.

src.label: North Dakota Secretary of State, 2026 general election key information

dates.label: Absentee ballots must arrive
dates.detail: An absentee ballot must be received by your county auditor by the close of polls. You can mail it, hand-deliver it to the auditor, or use a county drop box. Polling places do not take absentee ballots.
